data.name: Introduction: Wrath of the Lich King
entries: Icecrown Citadel is the seat of the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King's} power. Towering above the frozen wastes of Northrend, the fortress is carved from the crystallized blood of an Old God and reinforced with unimaginable necromantic power. Icecrown Citadel serves as both throne and factory, where souls are transformed into weapons of undeath and the Lich King commands {@book the Scourge|WoW|6|The Scourge} to spread across Azeroth, devouring all in its path.

Introduced as the climactic raid to the {@i Wrath of the Lich King} expansion to the {@i World of Warcraft} MMORPG, Icecrown Citadel brings the storyline of that expansion to a world-shattering conclusion as raids of ten or twenty-five characters at the peak of their powers fought their way through eleven bosses before confronting Arthas in his lair and bringing about his fall.

This adventure translates the epic experience of the MMO raid into a tabletop experience using the rules in {@book D&D: World of Warcraft|WoW}. Designed for a party of five characters, the adventure challenges characters at the pinnacle of their careers. Level 16 characters who enter the dungeon can, over the course of exploring the four major sections of the citadel and defeating the mighty lieutenants of the Lich King, reach level 20 and face Arthas at the Frozen Throne.

entries.name: Using This Adventure
entries: To run this adventure, you need the fifth edition core rulebooks: the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}, the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}, and the {@book Monster Manual|XMM}. You also need the {@i D&D: World of Warcraft} sourcebook.
The assault on Icecrown Citadel begins in this introduction and unfolds in five chapters:

{@area Light's Hammer|007|x}. This introduction presents the foothold claimed by the Ashen Verdict at the entrance to Icecrown Citadel. It introduces quest givers and other NPCs, rewards characters can gain, and the Scourge forces that continually assail the attackers gathered here.

{@adventure The Lower Spire|ICC|1}. Chapter 1 covers characters' first incursion into the citadel, as they face first Lord Marrowgar at the spire's base and then the death cultists of Lady Deathwhisper in the Oratory of the Damned. They can then ascend to the Rampart of Skulls to prepare to assault the upper levels. Characters should be level 16 when they begin this chapter and reach level 17 at the end of it.

{@adventure The Plagueworks|ICC|2}. In chapter 2, characters journey from the Rampart of Skulls to Deathbringer's Rise and navigate a painful reunion between Horde leader Varok Saurfang and his son Dranosh, who is now a powerful death knight in the Lich King's service. They can then enter the upper spire of the citadel and confront the Scourge abominations in the Plagueworks, including Professor Putricide. Characters reach level 18 after clearing the Plagueworks.

{@adventure The Crimson Hall|ICC|3}. In chapter 3, characters make their way around the upper reaches and discover the sanctuary of the San'layn, elf vampires under the Lich King's command. The characters must defeat the three vampires of the blood prince council before confronting Blood-Queen Lana'thel and reaching level 19.

{@adventure Frostwing Hall|ICC|4}. In chapter 4, characters complete their circuit of the upper reaches. First, they can free Valithria Dreamwalker, a dragon of the green dragonflight who is imprisoned by the Lich King's forces. Then they must face the undead dragons corrupted by the Scourge, including the Lich King's mount, Sindragosa. The characters reach level 20 by the end of this chapter.
{@adventure The Frozen Throne|ICC|5}. Finally, in chapter 5, the characters ascend to the Frozen Throne and face Lich King Arthas himself.

When a stat block name in the adventure text is followed by an asterisk (*), the stat block is found in {@adventure appendix A|ICC|6}. Other monster stat blocks referenced here appear in either the {@i Monster Manual} or {@i D&D: World of Warcraft}.
{@adventure Appendix B|ICC|7} contains rules for new magic items found in this adventure.

entries.name: Standalone Adventure
entries: You can run Icecrown Citadel as a standalone adventure. Have your players create level 16 characters using the rules in the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} and {@book D&D: World of Warcraft|WoW}. D&D Beyond can also help your players {@link quickly create characters of the appropriate level|https://www.dndbeyond.com/play/characters/build}.

Characters created at level 16 for this adventure have a {@book Renown Score|WoW|4} of 40 with their starting faction and a Renown Score of 10 with the {@book Argent Dawn|WoW|4|Argent Dawn}. One character—most likely a {@class death knight|WoW}, {@class paladin|WoW}, or {@class warrior|WoW}—also begins in possession of {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC} (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" later in this introduction).

entries.name: Campaign Climax
entries: Icecrown Citadel can serve as a dramatic conclusion for a {@i D&D: World of Warcraft} campaign, especially if the campaign has featured the battle against the Scourge as one of the major conflicts.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Icecrown Citadel is the stronghold of the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King}, the head of the Scourge (both {@book detailed|WoW|6|The Scourge} in {@i D&D: World of Warcraft}). After the Scourge's rampage through Lordaeron, the corruption of Arthas Menethil, and the fallen paladin's rise to become the new Lich King, the Scourge fell quiet for a few years. Unbeknownst to anyone outside of Icecrown Citadel, Arthas was biding his time—first bringing under his control the spirit of Ner'zhul that lived in his mind, then marshalling the strength of the Scourge to launch a new assault on Azeroth. As a paladin, Arthas had sought to bring order and justice to Azeroth. That desire remained in his frozen heart, but it was twisted.

A world ruled by the undead would have no more injustice, no more wars, no more mortal flaws. Perhaps more importantly to the Lich King, he believed his Scourge would be far more capable of defending Azeroth against all threats than mere mortals could ever be. A fractured world, constantly beset by skirmishes between the Alliance and the Horde, simply wouldn't be prepared for another incursion by either {@book the Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion} or the {@book forces of the Void|WoW|6|Old Gods}.

The Lich King had his strategy in place. He knew it wouldn't be enough to conquer the world through sheer force; many others had tried that and failed. To control Azeroth, the Lich King would instead enslave its mightiest champions—the heroes of the Alliance and the Horde. Once they bent to his will, the rest of the world would fall.

Five years after Ner'zhul's defeat in the Third War, the Scourge struck once more, launching brutal attacks against both the Alliance and the Horde. But these were mostly feints, designed to rouse anger and provoke the world's greatest champions to come to Northrend—within the Lich King's sinister reach.

entries.name: Battle of the Wrathgate
entries: As the Alliance and the Horde pushed into Northrend, two commanders rose to the fore. On the Alliance side, the paladin Bolvar Fordragon led the Valiance Expedition to Northrend and established a beachhead on the Howling Fjord. A young champion named Dranosh Saurfang commanded the Horde's Warsong Offensive, which made landfall in the Borean Tundra. As both armies pushed deeper inland toward the Lich King's citadel, they realized that their common goal was more important than their differences, and a grudging mutual respect formed between the two commanders. Eventually, the Alliance and Horde forces met at the southern entrance of Icecrown: Angrathar the Wrathgate.

Arthas led the Scourge forces on the field of battle outside the Wrathgate. The combined forces of the Alliance and the Horde proved mighty, and they might have secured victory against the Lich King, were it not for a horrific betrayal within the Horde.

From a rise overlooking the Wrathgate, a barrage of canisters pelted the battlefield, releasing a lethal green fog that killed the living and the undead alike. The Lich King retreated at once, but almost five thousand Alliance soldiers and over four thousand Horde soldiers fell, along with their commanders. Only the intervention of the red dragonflight prevented the plague from spreading beyond the battlefield and laying waste to the entire region. The dragons' flames eradicated the plague but couldn't save the fallen.

{@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW}, leader of the Forsaken, had ordered the creation of the deadly plague because she was so desperate to claim vengeance against the Lich King that she was willing to sacrifice anything to achieve it. She claimed that the plague was the act of Forsaken alchemists rebelling against her leadership, but the Alliance's King Varian Wrynn received her explanation with suspicion, and any hope of cooperation between the Alliance and the Horde was dashed.
When the smoke cleared, neither Bolvar nor Dranosh could be found. Both are now inside Icecrown Citadel, though their fates are very different.

entries.name: Brink of Victory
entries: Despite the terrible losses at the Wrathgate, the Alliance and the Horde crushed numerous Scourge outposts throughout Northrend, and their leaders now feel poised at the brink of victory. The Lich King seems to be holding most of his forces back in Icecrown Citadel, almost daring his enemies to storm it.

Indeed, {@creature Tirion Fordring|ICC}, the leader of the Argent Crusade, suspects the Lich King is hoping to lure armies into the citadel, knowing that the Scourge can absorb heavy losses. After all, every Alliance or Horde soldier that falls in an assault can be raised as a new soldier for the Scourge. Tirion believes there is only one way to conquer Icecrown Citadel: A small, surgical strike force could punch a hole in the citadel's defenses and fight its way to the Lich King.

To that end, Tirion has gathered the preeminent champions of Azeroth—the adventurers—to bring final judgment on the Lich King. Supporting their assault is the {@area Ashen Verdict|025|x}—a desperate partnership of the Argent Crusade with the Knights of the Ebon Blade, an order of death knights who have broken free of the Lich King's control and seek atonement for the evil deeds they perpetrated as part of the Scourge.

entries.name: Light's Hammer
entries: The adventure begins in Light's Hammer, the entryway to the Lich King's citadel. The Ashen Verdict has already battered open the gates to the citadel with a massive siege engine and established a foothold inside the citadel. That foothold serves as the characters' base of operations throughout the adventure.
Read this introduction to set the scene for the adventure:

The mountains of Icecrown form a vast fortress holding the war machine of the Lich King. Hordes of his Scourge minions are amassed on the fields of Icecrown. You entered Mord'rethar, the Murder Gate, and made your way through the bone-strewn Valley of Lost Hope. You passed through Aldur'thar, the Desolation Gate, and traversed the spirit-haunted Valley of Fallen Heroes. Lastly you fought through Corp'rethar, the Horror Gate, and entered the Court of Bones—the doorstep to Icecrown Citadel.

Leering dragon skulls look down on you from the buttresses that flank the gigantic staircase leading up to the citadel. Gargoyles perch on the battlements above, and the Lich King's banners hang at the base of the stairs, warning all who approach that they enter the heart of the Scourge's domain. The black fortress—constructed from saronite, the fossilized blood of an Old God—towers overhead, its prongs threatening to pierce the sky.

But the way has already been cleared. At the top of the stairs, knights of the Argent Crusade and the Ebon Blade stand guard against the gargoyles, geists, and pustulent horrors that periodically throw themselves against these intruders. And a mighty battering ram, adorned with the star-shaped insignia of the Argent Crusade, stands before the shattered gate leading into the Lich King's sanctum.
Beyond the gate, a long hallway, lined with skull-shaped braziers burning with eerie blue flame, leads to an inner gate.
The inner gate is closed but opens easily to admit the characters to Light's Hammer.

entries.name: Light's Hammer over Time
entries: When the characters first arrive at Icecrown Citadel, Light's Hammer is under siege. As the characters progress through the citadel, the Ashen Verdict secures a stronger hold over its camp.

entries.name: Besieged Encampment
entries: At the start of the adventure, Light's Hammer is a small foothold at the entrance to the citadel, under constant assault from the Lich King's forces. Elite soldiers from both the Argent Crusade and the Knights of the Ebon Blade maintain constant watch around the perimeter of the camp, fighting back intermittent attacks from The Damned—skeletal horrors with scythe-like claws in place of hands. Every 10 minutes, {@dice 1d3} of {@creature The Damned|ICC}* emerge from the room to the south and attack the guards in area H2, H5, or H8. (Roll {@dice 1d8} separately for each of The Damned: on a {@b 1–3}, The Damned goes west to H5; on a {@b 4–5}, it goes north toward H2; on a {@b 6–8}, it goes east to H8.) The guards destroy the attackers in {@dice 1d4 + 1} rounds.

entries.name: Safe Haven
entries: As described in {@adventure chapter 1|ICC|1}, the characters' assault beyond Light's Hammer signals the rest of the knights to strike out at the remaining undead haunting the lower spire. By the time the characters defeat {@creature Lady Deathwhisper|ICC} in area L3, the knights have transformed Light's Hammer into a safe haven. From that point on, the characters can rest there without interruption.

entries.name: Agony of Defeat
entries: Each chapter in this adventure features a series of encounters that range between moderate and high difficulty according to {@book the guidelines|XDMG|3|Combat Encounter Difficulty} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}. Even for characters at the pinnacle of their careers, defeat is a possibility.

The {@i Dungeon Master's Guide} offers suggestions for {@book what to do if all the characters die|XDMG|2|What If Everyone Dies?}. An additional possibility for this adventure is that the Lich King achieves his goal: He transforms the characters into his undead servants and forces them to lead the forces of the Scourge. Discuss with your players how the campaign proceeds from that point, considering the following options:

items: The characters join the Scourge and the curtain closes, ending the campaign.
Run ongoing adventures with the characters, now evil, helping the Scourge conquer the world.
Ask the players to describe some of the heinous evils they committed as part of the Scourge before being liberated by a momentary weakening of the Lich King's will, much like the Forsaken were freed.
Have the players create new characters whose ultimate goal will be to defeat their old characters—the new commanders of the Scourge.

entries.name: Light's Hammer Locations
entries: The vaulted ceilings of Light's Hammer are 40 to 50 feet high, giving ample room for even the Lich King's largest minions to pass through the space. The following locations are keyed to {@adventure map 0.1|ICC|0|Map 0.1: Light's Hammer}.

entries.name: H1: Entry Transporter

entries: Just where the hallway opens into the entry, an arcane sigil glows in the center of a circular frame set into the floor. Icy mist swirls across its surface.

Two Ashen Verdict commanders—a living human of the Argent Crusade (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Questing Knight|XMM}) and a night elf of the Ebon Blade (Medium, Lawful Neutral {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM})—keep watch here.

entries.name: Icecrown Citadel Transporters
entries: The glowing sigil is a teleportation device connected to similar sigils throughout the citadel. A character must take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate a transporter, making that transporter available as a destination. Once a character has activated a transporter as a destination, the character can take the Magic action while standing on any other transporter to teleport to that destination.
The other transporters are at the following locations:

items.name: L4:
items.entry: Oratory Transporter. This transporter is located outside the Oratory of the Damned in the lower spire (see {@area chapter 1|054|x}).

items.name: L7:
items.entry: Rampart of Skulls Transporter. This transporter is located near the lift leading up from the Oratory of the Damned (see {@area chapter 1|060|x}).

items.name: P1:
items.entry: Saurfang's Rise Transporter. This transporter is located at the landing to Saurfang's Rise (see {@area chapter 2|070|x}).

items.name: P4:
items.entry: Upper Spire Transporter. This transporter is located just beyond the Frozen Gatehouse (see {@area chapter 2|07e|x}).

items.name: F5:
items.entry: Sindragosa's Lair Transporter. This transporter is located in a hallway to the side of Sindragosa's Lair (see {@area chapter 4|0ce|x}).

entries.name: H2: Entry Chamber
entries: Read or paraphrase the following (adjust this text to account for the presence or absence of faction leaders as described below):

In a vast entry hall lit by eerie blue flames, the forces leading the assault on Icecrown Citadel are gathered. Highlord Tirion Fordring, leader of the Argent Crusade, holds his mighty blade Ashbringer as he confers with prominent faction leaders. Other soldiers are gathered nearby, including a formidable line of defense keeping skeletal horrors from breaking through. To the east, the haunting faces of the Ebon Blade are gathered, while the living but equally grim visages of Argent Crusade allies are camped to the west. Two smiths work noisily at forges nearby.

This chamber is the heart of the Ashen Verdict's assault on Icecrown Citadel. Its guards include three Argent Commanders (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Questing Knight|XMM|Questing Knights}) and three Ebon Blade Commanders (Medium, Lawful Neutral {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants}), plus {@creature Tirion Fordring|ICC}* and possibly Alliance leaders, Horde leaders, or both.

entries.name: Crafting Resources
entries: {@i D&D: World of Warcraft} includes rules for crafting items using resources characters collect on their adventures. Many of the treasure hoards in this adventure include such resources. Like trade goods, they have a monetary value, and that value can be applied directly to the cost of creating items, including magic items. See {@book chapter 3|WoW|3|Professions and Crafting} of {@i D&D: World of Warcraft} for details.

entries.name: Alliance and Horde
entries: In World of Warcraft, the battle against the Lich King is also a battle between the Alliance and the Horde, with one faction (the one the players belong to) forging an alliance with the Ashen Verdict and the other operating at odds with the players. The recent events at the Wrathgate (see "{@area Battle of the Wrathgate|005|x}" earlier in this introduction) have shattered the tenuous trust that was building between the factions, preventing them from cooperating.

In your game, if the player characters all belong to the same faction, you can preserve that element of the adventure. Alternatively, you can present the offensive against the Lich King as a joint effort, with the Alliance and the Horde setting aside their differences, or the heroes might be working with the Ashen Verdict independent of the warring factions. The following describes which leaders are present based on your approach:

items.name: Alliance-Led Effort
items.entry: King Varian Wrynn (or his son {@creature Anduin Wrynn|WoW|Anduin}, depending on the needs of your campaign) and King Muradin Bronzebeard stand alongside Highlord Tirion Fordring, with three human Alliance Commanders (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Questing Knight|XMM|Questing Knights}) protecting them.

items.name: Horde-Led Effort
items.entry: Garrosh Hellscream and High Overlord Varok Saurfang stand alongside Highlord Tirion Fordring, with three orc Kor'kron Generals (Medium, Chaotic Good {@creature Warrior Commander|XMM|Warrior Commanders}) protecting them.

items.name: Joint Effort
items.entry: Both the Alliance and Horde leaders are present with their guards.

items.name: Independent Effort
items.entry: No faction leaders are here; adjust the read-aloud text accordingly.

entries.name: Grimtong's Forge
entries: On the west side of the chamber, the tauren Crusader Grimtong works at his forge with the human Crusader Halford (both are Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Questing Knight|XMM|Questing Knights}). The two sell magic weapons and other items that can be made using {@book blacksmithing|WoW|3|Blacksmithing}, giving discounts based on renown with the Ashen Verdict.

entries.name: Ormus the Penitent's Forge
entries: On the east side of the chamber, the blind human death knight Ormus the Penitent works at his forge with his draenei apprentice, Aronen (both are Medium, Lawful Neutral {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants}). Seeking to atone for the sins he committed in the Lich King's service, Ormus forges magic rings for adventurers and other champions of the Ashen Verdict (see "{@area Ashen Verdict Renown|026|x}"). Ormus also sells magic Heavy armor, giving discounts based on renown with the Ashen Verdict.

entries.name: H3: Alchemist's Alcove

entries: Up a half-dozen stairs from the entry chamber to the west, an alcove holds a pavilion providing shelter to a handful of Ashen Verdict merchants and an Argent Crusade guard.
Three merchants offer goods here, protected by an Argent Commander (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Questing Knight|XMM}).

entries.name: Alchemist Finklestein
entries: A Forsaken member of the Argent Crusade is highly unusual, and Alchemist Finklestein (Medium, Chaotic Neutral {@creature Archmage|XMM} with the Undead type) seems both unwelcome and uncomfortable, even alongside the death knights in the chamber. He claims to be busy, though it's not clear what he's working on. He sells items that can be crafted using {@book alchemy|WoW|3|Alchemy}, giving discounts based on renown with the Ashen Verdict.

entries.name: Scott the Merciful
entries: Scott is a human priest (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Archpriest|XMM}) affiliated with the Argent Crusade. He offers spellcasting (from the spells available to {@class Priest|WoW|priests}) and has {@dice 1d6} random magic items for sale from the {@book Relics tables|XDMG|6|Relics Tables} in the Dungeon Master's Guide, giving discounts based on renown with the Ashen Verdict. He continually tries to engage Finklestein in friendly conversation, despite the alchemist's gruff distance.

entries.name: Goodman the "Closer"
entries: Goodman is a human (Medium {@creature Spy|XMM}) who has joined forces with the Ashen Verdict despite his shady past. He has {@dice 1d8} random magic items for sale from the {@book Implements tables|XDMG|6|Implements Tables} in the {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}, giving discounts based on renown with the Ashen Verdict. He fills awkward silences between Finklestein and Scott with random nattering or groan-worthy jokes.

entries.name: H4: Dalaran Portal

entries: A buttress supporting the wall and vaulted ceiling separates this portion of the western alcove from the area to the north. Through a glowing portal, the spires of Dalaran are visible. A human mage nearby checks the portal from time to time.

The mage, Malfus Grimfrost (Medium {@creature Archmage|XMM}), offers spellcasting (from the spells available to {@class Mage|WoW|mages}) and has {@dice 1d6} random magic items for sale from the {@book Arcana tables|XDMG|6|Arcana Tables} in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}, giving discounts based on renown with the Ashen Verdict. Characters who activate the portal with the {@action Magic|XPHB} action can freely use it to teleport to {@book Dalaran|WoW|4|Kirin Tor}.

If Dalaran has been destroyed in your campaign, the portal leads to another city of your choice. There might even be two portals here, with Malfus maintaining a portal to Stormwind and a Forsaken woman named Uvlus Banefire maintaining one to Orgrimmar.

entries.name: H5: Kunz's Tent

entries: At the southern end of the western alcove, four soldiers guard against the frequent approach of skeletal horrors. A pavilion provides them shelter.

Commander Kunz is in charge of the three Argent Crusade champions here. All four are Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Questing Knight|XMM|Questing Knights}. Kunz is a no-nonsense soldier with no patience for questions he perceives as a waste of time.

entries.name: H6: Torgo's Tent

entries: Up a half-dozen stairs from the entry chamber to the east, a morose, white-haired death knight sits alone in his tent.

This death knight is Torgo the Elder (Medium, Lawful Neutral {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM}), who—like many of the death knights associated with the Ashen Verdict—deeply regrets the evils he committed in the Lich King's service. Above all, Torgo wishes he could be reunited with his son, who was a teenager when Torgo was killed and raised into the Scourge.

entries.name: H7: Ebon Blade Command Post

entries: A buttress supporting the wall and vaulted ceiling separates this portion of the eastern alcove from the area to the north. A large pavilion serves as the command post for the leader of the Ebon Blade, whose undead warhorse stamps its feet impatiently nearby.

Highlord Darion Mograine (Medium, Lawful Neutral {@creature Death Knight|XMM}) and two Ebon Blade Commanders (Medium, Lawful Neutral {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants}) lean over a small table holding a sketch of Icecrown, discussing tactics for the battles raging outside the citadel. Mograine's steed, Fury, is an Undead {@b Otherworldly Steed} summoned with the {@spell Find Steed|XPHB} spell (level 4 version).

entries.name: H8: Vadu's Tent

entries: At the southern end of the eastern alcove, five soldiers guard against skeletal horrors. A pavilion provides them shelter.

Stefan Vadu is in charge of the four Ebon Blade champions here (Medium, Lawful Neutral {@creature Death Knight Aspirant|XMM|Death Knight Aspirants}). Vadu is a tormented death knight who is deeply troubled by the voice of the Lich King gnawing at his mind while he camps in Icecrown Citadel, and he is eager for this offensive to silence the Lich King's voice forever.

entries.name: Ashen Verdict
entries: The spearhead of the assault on Icecrown Citadel is the Ashen Verdict, a temporary alliance between the Argent Crusade (itself an outgrowth of the {@book Argent Dawn faction|WoW|4|Argent Dawn} described in {@i D&D: World of Warcraft}, united with the surviving paladins of the Order of the Silver Hand from fallen Lordaeron) and the Knights of the Ebon Blade, a band of renegade death knights freed from the control of the Lich King. The leaders of these two factions—Highlord {@creature Tirion Fordring|ICC} of the Argent Crusade and Highlord Darion Mograine of the Ebon Blade—are accompanied by their most trusted lieutenants and soldiers to maintain their foothold, called Light's Hammer, at the entrance to Icecrown Citadel.

entries.name: Ashen Verdict Renown
entries: By cooperating with the Ashen Verdict, characters can increase their Renown Score with the faction. By joining the assault on Icecrown Citadel, characters gain a Renown Score of 3 with the Ashen Verdict. Thanks to the involvement of the Knights of the Ebon Blade, characters with the {@book Oath of the Ebon Blade subclass|WoW|1|Oath of the Ebon Blade (Paladin Subclass)} increase their score by 1.

Increasing your Renown Score with the Ashen Verdict gives you the following benefits, in addition to the {@book general renown perks|WoW|4|General Renown Perks} described in {@i D&D: World of Warcraft}.

entries.name: Ashen Verdict: Friendly
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 3+ with the Ashen Verdict}

Ormus the Penitent, a death knight member of the Ashen Verdict, seeks to atone for the sins he committed in the Lich King's service by forging magic rings for his allies to use in the struggle against the Scourge. At the start of the adventure, he gives one of these rings—an {@i Ashen Band} of your choice (see {@adventure appendix B|ICC|7})—to you. As you gain renown with the Ashen Verdict, you can bring your ring back to Ormus, who improves it.
The first time your Renown Score with the Ashen Verdict reaches 3, increase your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn by 1.

entries.name: Ashen Verdict: Honored
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 10+ with the Ashen Verdict}
Ormus the Penitent improves your {@i Ashen Band} to Rare quality.
The first time your Renown Score with the Ashen Verdict reaches 10, increase your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn by 2.

entries.name: Ashen Verdict: Revered
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 25+ with the Ashen Verdict}
Ormus the Penitent improves your {@i Ashen Band} to Very Rare quality.
The first time your Renown Score with the Ashen Verdict reaches 25, increase your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn by 3.

entries.name: Ashen Verdict: Exalted
entries: {@i Prerequisite: Renown 50+ with the Ashen Verdict}
Ormus the Penitent improves your {@i Ashen Band} to Legendary quality.
The first time your Renown Score with the Ashen Verdict reaches 50, increase your Renown Score with the Argent Dawn by 5.

entries.name: Shadowmourne
entries: Highlord Darion Mograine, the leader of the Knights of the Ebon Blade, suggests that the characters might have an easier time defeating Arthas if they wield his former weapon against him. With some trepidation, he offers to combine various elements gathered by the characters into a mighty weapon. The process involves first transforming Arthas's mighty maul into a magic axe called {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}, which can then be improved until it reaches its final form: {@item Shadowmourne|ICC}.

entries.name: Quests and Adventure Structure
entries: The quests that allow the party to create {@i Shadowmourne}, as well as the promise of improved {@i Ashen Bands}, provide the adventure's structure. The need to return to Light's Hammer for Ormus and Darion to do their work gives characters a clear incentive to pause and rest between chapters of the adventure. The citadel's transporters allow the characters to easily teleport to Light's Hammer, rest, and then return to where they left off.

entries.name: The Sacred and the Corrupt
entries: The first step toward forging {@i Shadowmourne} is to retrieve Arthas's discarded hammer, {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC}, from Frostmourne Cavern, where Arthas first took up the sword {@item Frostmourne|WoW} instead. If you're playing this adventure as a standalone event, assume one of the characters already carries {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC}. Otherwise, when the characters meet Darion Mograine (see {@area area H7 above|021|x}), he charges them with a mission:

"It is against my judgment that I present you this errand," the death knight says, "as it will likely end in your undoing. But if you decide to take on this task, I shall provide you with knowledge and resources to see it through.
First, you must venture to Frostmourne Cavern to recover Light's Vengeance, Arthas's discarded hammer."

The characters can leave the citadel, journey to the base of the glacier in the northern part of the Dragonblight, and find the cave. Inside, the disembodied voice of the Lich King taunts them as seemingly innumerable {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls} (approximately fifty of them, but more arise to ensure the characters feel threatened until they activate {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC}) arise from the ice to prevent the characters from claiming the hammer:

"So predictable," Arthas's voice says. "Did you truly expect to fulfill Mograine's task unopposed? You shall all suffer as his father does—in eternal unrest! Die well, fools." The ghouls close in on you as a ray of sunlight falls on the hammer, half-buried in the snow.

The first time a {@class Fighter|XPHB} or {@class Paladin|WoW} (including a {@class death knight|WoW}) touches {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC}, the Artifact immediately activates its Repel Undead property (see {@adventure appendix B|ICC|7}). Assume all the ghouls fail their saving throw and are either destroyed or repelled, allowing the characters to escape the cave with the weapon.
When the characters bring {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC} to Highlord Mograine, he points them to the items required to begin the reforging of the weapon:

So, it has begun. From this weapon of the Light we shall forge the Lich King's doom, a weapon of untold potential. Reforged with saronite and etched with the acidic venom of his high priests, it will provide the foundation for our work.

He instructs the characters to return to him with five shards of primordial saronite and two flasks of venom taken from Undead nerubians. The characters can acquire these items in {@adventure chapter 1|ICC|1}.

entries.name: Shadow's Edge
entries: When the characters return to Highlord Mograine with the required items, his runeforge's flame burns ravenously. Read or paraphrase the following:

"Behold!" the death knight rasps. "The binding of sacred and corrupt: the forging of Shadow's Edge. Bend it to your will, and you shall wield unstoppable power! Fail, and your soul shall be forever bound to the blade."
After an hour of work, Highlord Mograine transforms {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC} into {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}. He gives the new weapon to the characters with a dire warning:

Listen well. In accepting this weapon, your fate is sealed. Overcome or succumb. I have placed your feet upon this path. You are therefore my personal responsibility. Should you falter, I am duty bound to deliver you from this life. Remember my words, and do not fail.

entries.name: Unholy Infusion
entries: After {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC} has transformed into {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}, Highlord Mograine's next instructions lead the characters into {@adventure chapter 2|ICC|2}:

Before your weapon can reach its full potential, it must be endowed with its signature powers. First among them is unholiness. You must seek out and defeat the one called Professor Putricide, but his death is not your only goal. You must use his resources against him. Find a way to absorb his mutated slime. Use the foul substance to infuse your weapon with the power of the unholy. When this is done, I shall reveal your next task.

{@area Area P9 in chapter 2|096|x} describes how to infuse the slime's power into {@i Shadow's Edge}. Once this is done, the weapon gains the properties described in "Unholy Infusion" in {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC|the Artifact's description} in appendix B.

entries.name: Blood Infusion
entries: After the characters return from their encounter with {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide}, Highlord Mograine's next instructions lead the characters to {@adventure chapter 3|ICC|3}:

Your weapon is now prepared to be endowed with the power of blood. You must face Blood-Queen Lana'thel in battle and subject yourself to her Blood Mirror. This power will cause Shadow's Edge to drink the blood of the nearest living being. That being would be you. Once the blade's thirst is quenched, give the queen an ignominious death.

{@area Area C4 in chapter 3|0b0|x} describes the effects of {@creature Blood-Queen Lana'thel|ICC|Lana'thel's} Blood Mirror on the wielder of {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}. Once this task is complete, the weapon gains the properties described in "Blood Infusion" in {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC|the Artifact's description} in appendix B.

entries.name: Frost Infusion
entries: After the characters return from their encounter with Blood-Queen Lana'thel, Highlord Mograine's next instructions lead the characters to {@adventure chapter 4|ICC|4}:

Shadow's Edge is prepared to receive its final infusion of power. Sindragosa, the enemy's own mount, must fall. But before she is brought down, you must withstand her frozen breath without tasting death. Without his dragon, nothing shall stand between you and the Lich King.

{@area Area F4 in chapter 4|0c9|x} describes {@creature Sindragosa|ICC} and her Frost Breath's effect on the wielder of {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}. Once the Artifact is infused with frost and Sindragosa is slain, the weapon gains the properties described in "Frost Infusion" in {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC|the Artifact's description} in appendix B.

entries.name: The Splintered Throne
entries: After the characters return from their encounter with Sindragosa, Highlord Mograine presents the final quest necessary to transform the fully empowered {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} into {@item Shadowmourne|ICC}:

The Lich King's throne once served as his prison. Kil'jaeden himself crafted the throne out of icy crystals from the Twisting Nether. Its sole purpose was to hold the vengeful spirit of Ner'zhul, the first Lich King. When Arthas struck the crystal with Frostmourne, he released Ner'zhul's soul, allowing it to merge with his own. Splinters from that impact are now scattered throughout the citadel. The last pieces we need are used as weapons by the val'kyr who block your passage to Arthas's sanctum. Bring them to me.
{@area Area P5 in chapter 2|080|x} describes the val'kyr guardians and the weapons they wield.

entries.name: Shadowmourne
entries: When the characters return to Highlord Mograine with the val'kyr's weapons, he returns the weapon to his runeforge with the additional blades:

"It is complete," the death knight says. "Where most would falter, you have overcome." He places the mighty axe into his runeforge, which roars with blue flame. "You have withstood all the minions of the Lich King, and now Shadowmourne is yours—a newly forged weapon already steeped in this world's history, reborn into an unrivaled destiny. With this weapon you bear a solemn responsibility, and the time to carry out that charge is at hand. Take this weapon of myth and legend, and march on the Prince of Darkness. Avenge the countless heroes lost in his merciless campaign. Bring rest to their tortured souls."
The highlord steps away from the forge, and the weapon floats out from it to hover above his open hands.
Steel yourself, and guide Shadowmourne to fulfill the purpose of its creation.
The Artifact is no longer {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}, but {@item Shadowmourne|ICC}.

data.name: Chapter 1: The Lower Spire
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 16 Characters}

entries.name: Quests and Objectives
entries: The characters have the following tasks to complete in this chapter:

items.name: Clear an Extraction Point
items.entry: The characters must clear the {@area Rampart of Skulls|062|x} of danger so an airship can dock there. A lift in the {@area Oratory of the Damned|056|x} leads up to the Rampart of Skulls. Once the rampart is cleared, an airship carries the characters to the pinnacle of the spire.

items.name: Lord Marrowgar Must Die!
items.entry: A bone wraith called {@creature Lord Marrowgar|ICC} prevents access to the upper reaches of Icecrown Citadel. The characters must destroy this sentinel.

items.name: Deprogramming
items.entry: The Cult of the Damned—living cultists devoted to the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King} and the idea of undeath—has a temple within the citadel, where the lich {@creature Lady Deathwhisper|ICC} preaches a message of undead salvation to the cultists. Darnavan, a spy sent by the Argent Crusade to infiltrate the Cult of the Damned, is still among them and must be kept alive for questioning.

items.name: Shadow's Edge
items.entry: To forge {@item Light's Vengeance|ICC} into {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}, Highlord Mograine needs five shards of primordial saronite and two flasks of venom taken from Undead nerubians—items that can be found in the encounters in this chapter.

entries.name: Beginning the Chapter
entries: {@creature Tirion Fordring|ICC} spells out the characters' objectives, described above. Then the adventure begins in earnest when the characters leave Light's Hammer and make their way toward the spire. At that point, Tirion makes a rousing speech to the assembled Ashen Verdict:

This is our final stand. What happens here will echo through the ages. Regardless of the outcome, they will know that we fought with honor—that we fought for the freedom and safety of our people! Remember, heroes, fear is your greatest enemy in these befouled halls. Steel your hearts, and your souls will shine brighter than a thousand suns. The enemy will falter at the sight of you. They will fall as the light of righteousness envelops them! Our march upon Icecrown Citadel begins now!

Two of {@creature The Damned|ICC}* stand sentry at the exit from {@area Light's Hammer|007|x} (L1 on map 1). Their destruction signals the beginning of the Ashen Verdict's attack on Icecrown Citadel. The NPCs in Light's Hammer wait for the characters to destroy these undead before taking any action.
Defeating the Damned increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 1.

entries.name: The Lower Spire

images.title: Map 1: Lower Spire and Rampart of Skulls

entries: The spire is the frozen heart of Icecrown Citadel, stretching hundreds of feet from its bottom floor to the Frozen Throne at its apex. The bottom tier extends as high as the Rampart of Skulls, an open-air ring around the spire.

entries.name: Lower Spire Features
entries: Unless otherwise specified, the lower spire has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: The spire ({@area area L3|04b|x}) is an open shaft that rises hundreds of feet from the floor to the upper reaches ({@area described in chapter 2|06a|x}). Characters attempting to fly up the inside of the spire face multiple challenges. The column of unholy ice that rises through the center of the spire emits a freezing fog that makes the air in the spire {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. A creature flying through the fog makes a {@dc 22} Constitution saving throw at the start of each of its turns, gaining 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level on a failed save. Finally, two {@creature Val'kyr Herald|ICC|Val'kyr Heralds}* fly around the upper spire and fight any intruders. (All that said, if characters are determined to fly or teleport to the upper spire, bypassing the Rampart of Skulls and the short airship ride to {@area Saurfang's Rise|072|x}, they can—that freedom is one of the key differences between a tabletop RPG and a digital one.)
The vaulted ceiling in the Oratory of the Damned rises to a height of 50 feet.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The characters' progress through the dungeon is unimpeded by doors. Saronite doors in various places lead into labyrinthine halls that are beyond the scope of this adventure. These doors can't be opened while the will of the Lich King holds them closed.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Braziers of blue flame fill the lower spire with {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Lower Spire Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 1.

entries.name: L2: Lower Spire Entrance

entries: A flight of stairs leads up to a high platform where two skeletal figures stand guard. An enormous arachnoid monster is descending from the ceiling on a thread of webbing as you approach.
Three servants of the Lich King guard the entry to the lower spire: a {@creature Nerubian Crypt Fiend|WoW}, one of {@creature The Damned|ICC},* and a {@creature Servant of the Throne|ICC}.*

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating all three guardians increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 1. The crypt fiend lacks sufficient venom to extract for the purposes of forging {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction).

entries.name: L3: The Spire

entries: You stand at the base of an enormous, hollow tower stretching up farther than you can clearly see. A faintly glowing column of blue ice rises up the center of the tower, its base taking up most of this circular room. High above, you can see hanging braziers burning with blue flames; massive chains; metal supports; and an icy, opaque fog a hundred feet up.

Guarding the room is an enormous skeletal creature that floats about six feet off the floor, hovering above a swirling cloud of icy mist. Four enormous skulls bob above a massive ribcage with bone-shard blades protruding from the back. Huge claws resembling wings extend from its shoulder blades, and it wields a massive axe formed from shards of magical ice.
"This is the beginning and the end, mortals," the creature says. "None may enter the master's sanctum!"

This is {@creature Lord Marrowgar|ICC},* the first boss of Icecrown Citadel, a bone wraith crafted by the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King} from the remains of a thousand vanquished adventurers. Marrowgar wields the power of the Frozen Throne for the sole purpose of protecting the Lich King's sanctum from the unworthy, and it fights to the death.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating Lord Marrowgar increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2. Marrowgar's death also causes the ice blocking the ramps on either side of his chamber to break apart, allowing access to the Oratory Transporter and the {@area Oratory of the Damned|056|x} beyond.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: When Marrowgar is destroyed, two fragments skitter clear of the heap of bones. One is a {@item Fragment of Frozen Bone|ICC}. The other is a sliver of unmelting ice that functions as a {@item Pearl of Power|XDMG}. Three diamonds (worth 5,000 GP each) also clatter free of the shards of Marrowgar's axe. In addition, two shards of primordial saronite (mining resources worth 2,500 GP each; see the "{@area Crafting Resources|013|x}" sidebar in the introduction) stand out among the shattered ice near the ramps leading up to area L4.

entries.name: More Marrowgar Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Lord Marrowgar by interjecting some of the things it says in the WoW raid:
{@b At the Start of Combat.} "The Scourge will wash over this world as a swarm of death and destruction!"
{@b When Its Bone Storm Trait Deals Damage.} "BONE STORM!"
{@b When It Uses Its Bone Spike Graveyard Action.} "The only escape is death!"
{@b If a Character Drops to 0 Hit Points.} "More bones for the offering!"
{@b When It Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.} "The master's rage courses through me!"
{@b When It Dies.} "I see... only darkness."

entries.name: L4: Oratory Transporter

entries: An arcane sigil in a circular frame, identical to the one at the citadel's entrance, seems to stir with life as you reach the top of the ramp.
This transporter works exactly like the one in {@area area H1|00e|x}.

entries.name: L5: Oratory of the Damned

entries: A booming voice fills this room, and you quickly spot its source—an enormous lich, floating a few feet off the floor, draped in robes, wearing an elaborate headdress and a veil, and encircled by massive chains that float around her body. She is flanked by two towering nerubian priests. She speaks to several living people gathered before her.
"You have found your way here," she says, "because you are among the few gifted with true vision."

This is {@creature Lady Deathwhisper|ICC},* the Supreme Overseer of the Cult of the Damned. She is attended by two {@creature Deathspeaker High Priest|ICC|Deathspeaker High Priests},* five {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers}, and four {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics}. One of the berserkers is Darnavan, whom the characters have been ordered to extract for questioning.
If the characters don't interrupt her by initiating combat, Lady Deathwhisper continues with her exhortation of the cultists gathered before her:

You can see through the fog that hangs over this world like a shroud, and grasp where true power lies. Fix your eyes upon your crude hands: the sinew, the soft meat, the dark blood coursing within. It is a weakness, a crippling flaw—a joke played by the Creators upon their own creations. The sooner you come to accept your condition as a defect, the sooner you will find yourselves in a position to transcend it. Through our Master, all things are possible. His power is without limit, and his will unbending. Those who oppose him will be destroyed utterly, and those who serve—who serve wholly, unquestioningly, with utter devotion of mind and soul—will be elevated to heights beyond your ken.

If the characters initiate combat with any of the creatures in the room, Lady Deathwhisper ends her sermon and joins the fray. Otherwise, the characters can interact with her as they wish. She is implacable in her devotion to the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King} and responds to any threat or attempt at coercion by commanding her underlings to deal with these intruders.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating Lady Deathwhisper increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2. If they return Darnavan alive to {@area Light's Hammer|007|x}, their Renown Score increases by an additional 1.

In addition, Lady Deathwhisper's death activates the lift connecting her temple to area L6. The lift spends 1 minute descending 100 feet to the floor of the temple, remains there for another minute, then spends 1 minute ascending to the rampart, waits another minute, and continues this cycle indefinitely. The lift is a metal disk 25 feet in diameter that magically raises and lowers without any visible support or mechanism.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Lady Deathwhisper wears a {@item Ring of Maddening Whispers|ICC}. Three shards of primordial saronite (mining resources worth 2,500 GP each; see the "{@area Crafting Resources|013|x}" sidebar in the introduction) and six black sapphires (worth 5,000 GP each) are concealed in her pockets. In addition, a character can spend 1 minute to extract a flask of nerubian venom from each of the nerubian priests for use in forging {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction). Each of the two priests also wears an elaborate gold {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB} set with rubies worth 7,500 GP.

entries.name: More Deathwhisper Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Lady Deathwhisper by interjecting some of the things she says in the WoW raid:
{@b At the Start of Combat.} "What is this disturbance? You dare trespass upon this hallowed ground? This shall be your final resting place!"
{@b When She Uses Her Dominate Mind Bonus Action.} "You are weak, powerless to resist my will!"
{@b When She Casts {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB}.} "Arise, and exult in your pure form!"
{@b When Her Mana Shield Falls.} "Enough! I see I must take matters into my own hands!"
{@b If a Character Drops to 0 Hit Points.} "Do you yet grasp the futility of your actions?"
{@b When She Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.} "This charade has gone on long enough."
{@b When She Dies.} "All part of the master's plan... Your end is inevitable..."

entries.name: L6: Rampart of Skulls Transporter

entries: An arcane sigil in a circular frame, identical to the one at the citadel's entrance, seems to stir with life as you step off the magical lift.
This transporter works exactly like the one in {@area area H1|00e|x}.

entries.name: L7: Rampart of Skulls

entries: The oppressiveness of the citadel's interior gives way to the biting cold of the Northrend air. You have come to a rampart that encircles the spire, which continues hundreds more feet above you—but a perfect place for an airship to dock if you can clear a path.

Optionally, if you want to highlight the Alliance–Horde conflict that appears in the original adventure, the characters might find Alliance and Horde forces battling each other here. The Alliance forces consist of three {@creature Questing Knight|XMM|Questing Knights} and one {@creature Archpriest|XMM}. The Horde forces consist of four {@creature Warrior Commander|XMM|Warrior Commanders} and one {@creature Archmage|XMM}. They are battling when the characters arrive, and members of the characters' faction plead with them for help. Once the enemy forces are defeated, the survivors point the characters in the direction of their faction's airship—the Alliance gunship {@i Skybreaker} to the west or the Horde gunship {@i Orgrim's Hammer} to the east.

In any case, before the characters can reach the airship that waits for them, they must fight their way past the Lich King's defenses: an {@creature Abomination|WoW}, a {@creature Frost Wyrm|ICC},* and three {@creature Gargoyle|XMM|Gargoyles}.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating the Lich King's guardians increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 1. If you include an Alliance versus Horde battle, defeating the enemy soldiers increases each character's Renown Score with their faction by 3.

entries.name: Ending the Chapter
entries: When the characters safely board the airship, award them each 9,800 XP. (Alternatively, advance each character to level 17.) In addition, each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} increases by 3.

entries.name: Interlude: Airship Ascent
entries: The airship can bring the characters from the Rampart of Skulls to {@area Saurfang's Rise|072|x} in minutes, climbing several hundred feet while circling the spire once, bypassing the middle section of the spire. The airship differs based on which faction or factions lead the effort to assault Icecrown, as described below:

items.name: Alliance-Led Effort
items.entry: The Alliance gunship Skybreaker is commanded by Muradin Bronzebeard, High Thane of the Bronzebeard clan. A marvel of engineering, the gunship is held aloft and maneuvered by several powerful propeller engines and armed with many cannons and battery guns.

items.name: Horde-Led Effort
items.entry: The Horde gunship Orgrim's Hammer is commanded by Varok Saurfang, the father of the Warsong Offensive commander, Dranosh Saurfang. The ship is held aloft by two enormous zeppelins, and its prow is carved to look like a wolf's head, with its mouth holding the barrels of the ship's forward guns.

items.name: Joint Effort
items.entry: The Alliance gunship Skybreaker carries the characters along with both Muradin and Varok.

items.name: Independent Effort
items.entry: A zeppelin—the Cloudkisser, captained by a goblin named Cryoflight—carries the characters up the spire. Sky-Captain Cryoflight is affiliated with the {@book Steamwheedle Cartel|WoW|4|Steamwheedle Cartel}, and she usually ferries passengers between Tirisfal Glades and the Howling Fjord.

entries: You can treat the airship ascent as nothing more than a narrative device moving the characters from point A to point B. They're sure to notice the {@creature Frost Wyrm|ICC|frost wyrms} flying around the upper reaches of the spire, providing a warning about that threat. The characters reach Saurfang's Rise without incident, if you so choose, beginning {@adventure chapter 2|ICC|2}.

However, if you want to retain the element of rivalry between the Alliance and the Horde, this journey can be complicated by the interference of the rival faction. In this case, both the Alliance gunship {@i Skybreaker} and the Horde gunship {@i Orgrim's Hammer} ascend together, and the captains of the vessels start shouting threats at each other. These threats escalate quickly into combat.

The ships fire their cannons at each other as each captain tries to force their rival to retreat. The enemy ship then sends a boarding party onto the characters' ship. If the characters have established rivals in the enemy faction, the boarders can be these rivals. Otherwise, use a party identical to the optional encounter on the Rampart of Skulls ({@area area L7|062|x}). The boarders teleport onto the deck and engage the characters in combat. The boarders wear parachutes and jump off the ship when defeat is imminent, rather than fighting to the death.
If the characters repel the boarders, the enemy ship retreats, and the characters can land safely at Saurfang's Rise, beginning {@adventure chapter 2|ICC|2}.

data.name: Chapter 2: The Plagueworks
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 17 Characters}

entries.name: Quests and Objectives
entries: The characters have the following tasks to complete in this chapter:

items.name: Access the Upper Spire
items.entry: The characters need to get into the upper spire and find a way from there to the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King's} {@adventure Frozen Throne|ICC|5}.

items.name: Prevent Another Plague
items.entry: {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide}, an undead alchemist in the Lich King's service, is working to create a plague that will destroy all life on Azeroth, and he must be stopped.

items.name: Unholy Infusion
items.entry: To infuse {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} with unholy power, the characters need to instill some of Professor Putricide's slime into the blade.

entries.name: Beginning the Chapter
entries: Reaching the transporter in {@area area P1|070|x} allows the characters to pause after the action of chapter 1. They can use the transporter to return to {@area Light's Hammer|007|x}, take a Long Rest if they wish to, and give Highlord Mograine the resources he needs to forge {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction).

While they rest, Alchemist Finklestein (see {@area area H3|017|x} in the introduction) approaches them. Finklestein has learned that {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide}, an undead alchemist in the Lich King's service, is studying the effects of the plague unleashed at the Wrathgate (see "{@area Battle of the Wrathgate|005|x}" in the introduction). Finklestein suspects that Putricide could be creating a plague that will destroy all life on Azeroth and asks the characters to stop the professor.

When they are fully rested, the characters can then use the entry transporter ({@area area H1|00e|x}) to return to the upper spire and continue their assault. The airship that carried the characters to the rise waits for them there.
Chapter 2 begins in earnest when the characters approach {@area area P2|072|x}.

entries.name: The Upper Spire

images.title: Map 2: Saurfang's Rise, Upper Spire, and Plagueworks

entries: Hundreds of feet above the main entry into the lower spire, the upper reaches of the spire are home to some of the Lich King's most important ongoing projects.

entries.name: Upper Spire Features
entries: Unless otherwise specified, the upper spire has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Ceilings throughout the upper spire are 30 feet high.

The central spire ({@area area P5|080|x}) is an open shaft, continuing from {@area area L3|04b|x} in the lower spire. Here the spire rises another 100 feet to the very top of the spire, but there is no access to the {@adventure Frozen Throne|ICC|5} from inside the spire. Two {@creature Val'kyr Herald|ICC|Val'kyr Heralds}* fly around the spire, discouraging anyone from taking to the air.

entries.name: Doors
entries: The characters' progress through the dungeon is unimpeded by doors. Saronite doors in various places lead into labyrinthine halls that are beyond the scope of this adventure. These doors can't be opened while the will of the Lich King holds them closed.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Braziers of blue flame fill the upper spire with {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Upper Spire Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 2.

entries.name: P1: Saurfang's Rise Transporter

entries: An arcane sigil in a circular frame, identical to the one at the citadel's entrance, seems to stir with life as you disembark the airship.
This transporter works exactly like the one in {@area area H1|00e|x}.

entries.name: P2: Saurfang's Rise

entries: Up a few steps from this landing, a heavy double door adorned with the image of a dragon's massive skull offers a way into the upper spire, but there is no obvious way to open the door.

When one character reaches the top step, the double door bursts open with a blast of icy wind and magical force that fills a 40-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from the door. Each creature in the Cone makes a {@dc 18} Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 55 ({@dice 10d10}) Cold damage, is pushed 20 feet directly away from the door, and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.
{@creature Deathbringer Saurfang|ICC}* stands in the open doorway and taunts the characters:
An orc death knight stands in the open doorway, gripping a greataxe, his eyes glowing blue in his dead-gray face. He chuckles.

With every Horde and Alliance soldier that has fallen in this pointless squabble of yours, the Lich King's armies have grown. Even now the val'kyr work to raise your fallen as Scourge. Things are about to get much worse. Taste the power the Lich King has bestowed on me!

Alternatively, if High Overlord Varok Saurfang is with the characters (as the commander of the Horde gunship {@i Orgrim's Hammer}), Deathbringer Saurfang instead invites Varok to join him in the Lich King's service:
Join me, father. Join me and we will crush this world in the name of the Scourge—for the glory of the Lich King!
The high overlord shakes his head sadly. "My boy died at the Wrathgate," he says. "I am here only to collect his body."
"Stubborn and old," the death knight replies. "What chance do you have? I am stronger and more powerful than you ever were."

As soon as combat begins, five blood beasts (use the {@creature Vampire Spawn|XMM} stat block) appear around Deathbringer Saurfang. Each of these vampiric creatures resembles an enormous leech with a toothy maw and a fin-ridged back and pulls itself around with its arms.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating Deathbringer Saurfang increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2. If Varok Saurfang is present, he weeps over the body of his son and then takes the corpse away, promising to give Dranosh a proper burial.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A saronite chest just inside the door contains the deathbringer's cache of treasure. It holds a {@item Bloodvenom Blade|ICC}, a set of {@item Goblin Jumper Cables|WoW}, five shards of primordial saronite ({@book mining|WoW|3|Mining} resources worth 2,500 GP each), five bolts of frostweave cloth (worth 500 GP each and useful for {@book tailoring|WoW|3|Tailoring} patterns), a platinum pendant with emeralds (worth 7,500 GP), and three frost lotus flowers (rare {@book herbalism|WoW|3|Herbalism} resources worth 2,500 GP each). (See the "{@area Crafting Resources|013|x}" sidebar in the introduction.)

entries.name: More Saurfang Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Deathbringer Saurfang by interjecting some of the things he says in the WoW raid:
{@b At the Start of Combat.} "By the might of the Lich King!"
{@b When He Uses His Mark of the Fallen Champion Bonus Action.} "The ground runs red with your blood!"
{@b If a Character Drops to 0 Hit Points.} "Your soul will find no redemption here!"
{@b When He Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.} "I have become... death!"
{@b When He Dies.} "I... am... released."

entries.name: P3: The Frozen Gatehouse

entries: Inside the double door, jets of freezing mist spew from nozzles in the walls every few seconds. The hall comes to a T, forcing you to the left or the right through a gauntlet of those frozen mists.

Characters must pass two sets of mist jets as they move north between the door and the T in the passage, then three more in each direction—one blocking their passage to the west or east, a second blocking their way north, and a third blocking their way back to the center and area P4. Avoiding the jets is easy; a character who waits for a blast to dissipate and then moves past that jet is unharmed. However, a character who tries to move past two sets of jets at a time is caught in the second set's blast.
A character caught in the frigid mists makes a {@dc 19} Constitution saving throw, taking 55 ({@dice 10d10}) Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: P4: Upper Spire Transporter

entries: An arcane sigil in a circular frame, identical to the one at the citadel's entrance, seems to stir with life as you pass the final wall of freezing mist.
This transporter works exactly like the one in {@area area H1|00e|x}.

entries.name: P5: The Upper Spire

entries: A stone walkway circles the inside of the upper spire here, which you have entered from the south. Similar archways lead out of the spire to the north, west, and east. Narrow walkways made of saronite metal lead from each archway to a circular platform at the center, surrounding a column of ice that rises all the way up the center of the towering spire. A small chamber is carved out of the ice, allowing passage through the column in all four directions.
To the west, two beacons blaze with sickly green flame halfway along the length of the saronite walkway. Two hideous Scourge abominations guard that archway.
To the east, similar beacons burn blue. You can see the flicker of red flames in reflections on the far side of the ice column, to the north.
From the platform and walkways, it is a drop of 300 feet to the floor below ({@area area L3|04b|x}).

This crossroads allows characters to head west into the Plagueworks ({@area area P6|083|x}), north into the {@adventure Crimson Hall|ICC|3}, or east into {@adventure Frostwing Hall|ICC|4}. If the characters are pursuing unholy power for {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction) or pursuing Alchemist Finklestein's lead (see "{@area Beginning the Chapter|069|x}"), they know they're looking for {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide}, and the {@creature Abomination|WoW|abominations} guarding area P6 are a strong pointer in that direction. If the characters ignore that signpost, they might face the encounters detailed in the next chapters before they are prepared for them, which could encourage the characters to retreat and seek Professor Putricide in the Plagueworks.

In the center of the ice column is another transporter similar to the ones scattered throughout the citadel. This one, however, doesn't show any signs of activity or respond to the characters' actions until the characters are ready to face the Lich King (see "Development" below).

Similarly, two {@creature Val'kyr Herald|ICC|Val'kyr Heralds}* patrol the spire, but they ignore characters who aren't flying until the characters complete chapters 2, 3, and 4. The spears wielded by the val'kyr heralds are topped with shadowfrost shards—fragments of the Frozen Throne. These are the final component used by Darion Mograine to transform Shadow's Edge into Shadowmourne (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction).

entries.name: Development
entries: When all of the bosses of Icecrown Citadel except the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King} have been slain ({@creature Lord Marrowgar|ICC}, {@creature Lady Deathwhisper|ICC}, {@creature Deathbringer Saurfang|ICC}, {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide}, {@creature Blood-Queen Lana'thel|ICC}, {@creature Sister Svalna|ICC}, and {@creature Sindragosa|ICC}) and the characters return here, the val'kyr move to intercept them before they reach the transporter. The transporter now responds to the characters and goes to only one destination: {@adventure the Frozen Throne|ICC|5}.

entries.name: P6: Plagueworks Entrance

entries: As you approach the western archway, you see two more Scourge horrors just behind the abominations. Sickly green flames cascade over a grotesque pillar behind these guards, and you see movement on the curving stairways that encircle the pillar, leading upward and beyond it.

The entrance to the Plagueworks is guarded by two {@creature Abomination|WoW|Abominations} and two {@creature Pustulating Horror|ICC|Pustulating Horrors}.* Ten {@creature Vengeful Geist|ICC|Vengeful Geists}* gambol around the ramps, joining the battle on the second round of combat.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating the entrance's guardians increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 1.

Beyond the entrance and the stairs encircling the pillar, the Plagueworks extend in three directions. Straight ahead to the west, a sealed door leads to {@area area P9|096|x}. A passage to the south turns to the west and leads into {@area area P7|086|x}, while a similar passage to the north turns west to {@area area P8|08e|x}. Huge glass pipes line the passage walls. Eight {@creature Vengeful Geist|ICC|Vengeful Geists}* clamber about above and behind the pipes in these halls, but they stay out of sight and don't initiate combat until a fight begins in area P7 or P8.

entries.name: P7: The Gas Lab

entries: Sickly orange gas fills this room. Eight huge vats of orange liquid around the outer wall of the room suggest the origin of this noxious vapor. In the center of the room, a misshapen abomination with extra and misplaced eyes, extraneous mouths and limbs, and crude staples holding its bloated form together plays with a similarly misshapen, gigantic dog. A frenzied voice emerges from a pipe, saying, "Just an ordinary gas cloud, but watch out because that's no ordinary gas cloud!"

This abomination is {@creature Festergut|ICC},* one of {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide's} prized creations, along with its treasured pet, a {@creature Plague-Dog|ICC}* named Stinky. Once combat begins, the eight {@creature Vengeful Geist|ICC|Vengeful Geists}* come in from the hallway (see {@area area P6|083|x}) and join the fray in the second round, unless the characters fought {@creature Rotface|ICC} in {@area area P8|08e|x} first and defeated the geists there. Festergut's Gaseous Blight trait makes the room dangerous to characters who enter, but the abomination's death causes the gas to dissipate.

entries.name: Development
entries: Professor Putricide watches the encounter unfold through a device in {@area area P9|096|x}, and a pipe carries his voice into this room.

A valve controlled by a wheel just inside the doorway to the north causes orange gas to flow into the pipes in the hallway. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to open the valve and send gas into these pipes. When gas from this room and slime from area P8 have both filled their respective pipes, the double door to area P9 opens.
Defeating Festergut increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2.

entries.name: Festergut Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Festergut by interjecting some of the things it says in the WoW raid:
{@b At the Start of Combat.} "Fun time?"
{@b When Stinky Dies.} "No! You killed Stinky! You pay!"
{@b When It Uses Its Pungent Blight Bonus Action.} "I not feel so good."
{@b If a Character Drops to 0 Hit Points.} "Daddy, I did it!"
{@b When It Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.} "Fun time over!"
{@b When It Dies.} "Dad... dy..."

entries.name: P8: The Slime Lab

entries: Eight huge vats of viscous green fluid line the outer wall of the room, and some of this slime drips from an open tap. In the center of the room, a misshapen abomination with extra and misplaced eyes, claws and fangs protruding from unexpected places, and extraneous limbs jutting from its bloated form clumsily pets a similarly misshaped, gigantic dog. A frenzied voice emerges from a pipe, saying, "Great news, everyone! The slime is flowing again!"

This abomination is {@creature Rotface|ICC},* one of {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide's} prized creations, which is accompanied by its treasured pet, a {@creature Plague-Dog|ICC}* named Precious. (True to its name, Precious wears a large red prize ribbon stapled to one shoulder.) Once combat begins, the eight {@creature Vengeful Geist|ICC|Vengeful Geists}* emerge from the hallway (see {@area area P6|083|x}) and join the fray in the second round, unless the characters fought {@creature Festergut|ICC} in {@area area P7|086|x} first and defeated the geists there.

entries.name: Development
entries: Professor Putricide watches the encounter unfold through a device in {@area area P9|096|x}, and a pipe carries his voice into this room.

A valve controlled by a wheel just inside the doorway to the south causes green slime to flow into the pipes in the hallway. A character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to open the valve and send slime into these pipes. When slime from this room and gas from area P7 have both filled their respective pipes, the double door to area P9 opens.
Defeating Rotface increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2.

entries.name: Rotface Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Rotface by interjecting some of the things it says in the WoW raid:
{@b At the Start of Combat.} "WEEEEEE!"
{@b When Precious Dies.} "What? Precious? Nooooooo!"
{@b When It Uses Its Slime Spray Action.} "Icky sticky!"
{@b If a Character Drops to 0 Hit Points.} "Daddy make toys out of you!"
{@b When It Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.} "Sleepy time!"
{@b When It Dies.} "Bad news, daddy..."

entries.name: P9: Professor Putricide's Laboratory of Alchemical Horrors and Fun
entries: The double door leading into the professor's laboratory is hydraulically sealed. It can be opened by turning the wheels in areas {@area P7|086|x} and {@area P8|08e|x}, channeling gas and slime into its opening mechanism. Once the door is open, read or paraphrase the following:

A towering Scourge figure in a filthy lab coat, with striking shocks of purple hair protruding from the sides of his otherwise bald head, stands near a table full of alchemical equipment. "You can't come in here all dirty like that!" he cries. "You need that nasty flesh scrubbed off first!"

This is {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide},* the mastermind behind the Plagueworks. Similar to the Forsaken, and unlike many of the mindless zombies and horrors that make up the Scourge, Professor Putricide retains his full intellectual capacity from life, now turning it toward increasing the efficiency of the plague of undeath and exterminating life on Azeroth.

entries.name: Mutated Slime
entries: During combat, Professor Putricide hurls vials of mutated slime to the ground that form rapidly expanding pools. These pools both threaten the characters and provide a means of empowering {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction).

A large flask on Putricide's table, with the words "Drink Me" written in large letters on its label, offers a solution to the slime pools. A character can drink the contents of the flask as a Bonus Action. Consuming the liquid causes the character to shape-shift into an abomination for 1 minute. The character's game statistics are replaced by the stat block of an {@creature Abomination|WoW}, but the character retains their alignment, personality, Hit Points, and Hit Point Dice. The character gains 168 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, and the effect ends early when the character has no Temporary Hit Points left. The character can't speak or cast spells, and their gear melds into the abomination form, so they can't use or otherwise benefit from any of that equipment.

While standing in a pool of Putricide's mutated slime, the shape-shifted character can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to eat some of the ooze—and in fact feels an unnatural curiosity to taste it. Eating the ooze has the following effects:

items.name: Ooze Power
items.entry: Until the end of the character's next turn, the abomination's Cleaver and Throw Flesh attacks deal Force damage instead of Necrotic damage.

items.name: Shrink Slime Pool
items.entry: The radius of the slime pool decreases by 10 feet. If its radius is reduced to 0 feet, the pool vanishes.

items.name: Unholy Empowerment
items.entry: If the shape-shifted character carried {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC}, the weapon is infused with unholy power.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating Professor Putricide increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Most of the alchemical equipment in the laboratory is contaminated with plague and should be destroyed. A few magic items are worthy of note: a {@item Tiny Abomination in a Jar|ICC} and two {@item Potion of Rejuvenation (Superior)|WoW|Potions of Rejuvenation} (superior). The laboratory also contains valuable resources useful in {@book alchemy|WoW|3|Alchemy} (see the "{@area Crafting Resources|013|x}" sidebar in the introduction): ten frost lotuses (rare {@book herbalism|WoW|3|Herbalism} resources worth 2,500 GP each), fifteen icecaps (herbalism resources worth 1,000 GP each), fifteen icethorns (herbalism resources worth 1,000 GP each), and ten shards of primordial saronite ({@book mining|WoW|3|Mining} resources worth 2,500 GP each).

In addition, a device resembling a large mirror on the west wall shows overhead views of areas P7 and P8, and pipes protruding from the walls on either side of the mirror carry sound from this room into those ones.

entries.name: More Putricide Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Professor Putricide by interjecting some of the things he says in the WoW raid:
{@b At the Start of Combat.} "Good news, everyone! I think I've perfected a plague that will destroy all life on Azeroth!"
{@b When His Unstable Mutation Triggers.} "Hmm. I don't feel a thing." (Then he notices his extra arms.) "Whaa...? Where'd those come from?"
{@b If a Character Drops to 0 Hit Points.} "That was unexpected!"
{@b When He Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB} in Phase 2.} "Great news, everyone!"
{@b When He Dies.} "Bad news, everyone... I don't think I'm going to make it..."

entries.name: Ending the Chapter
entries: When the characters defeat {@creature Professor Putricide, Phase 1|ICC|Professor Putricide} and destroy his plague apparatus, award them each 7,200 XP. (Alternatively, advance each character to level 18.) In addition, each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} increases by 3.

data.name: Chapter 3: The Crimson Hall
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 18 Characters}

entries.name: Quests and Objectives
entries: The characters have the following tasks to complete in this chapter:

items.name: Rescue Infiltrator Minchar
items.entry: A spy sent by the Argent Crusade to keep tabs on the San'layn has been captured and will be executed soon unless the characters can free him.

items.name: Decapitate the San'layn
items.entry: Elf vampires called the San'layn are coordinating Scourge offensives across Azeroth, so striking at their leadership in Icecrown Citadel will hamper the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King's} efforts.

items.name: Blood Infusion
items.entry: To infuse {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} with blood magic, the characters need to absorb some of {@creature Blood-Queen Lana'thel|ICC|Blood-Queen Lana'thel's} power into the blade.

entries.name: Beginning the Chapter
entries: After the characters rest from their efforts in chapter 2, an urgent message comes to Light's Hammer from a human scout of the Argent Crusade named Alrin the Agile (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Spy Master|XMM}).
