Alrin reports that another scout, a dwarf named Minchar, has been captured by the San'layn. Minchar is probably being tortured for information and will likely be executed soon. Alrin begs Highlord {@creature Tirion Fordring|ICC} to send help, and Tirion turns to the adventurers.

Tirion briefs the characters on the San'layn, vampiric blood elves in the Lich King's service. During the Third War, these elves were among the most loyal and powerful followers of Kael'thas Sunstrider, the prince of Quel'Thalas. Arthas defeated them and raised them to undeath, and they remain among his most powerful agents. Their leaders reside in the Crimson Hall, and Tirion requests that the adventurers turn their attention to these darkfallen elves, destroy their leadership, and retrieve poor Minchar from their clutches.
Chapter 3 begins when the characters enter {@area area C1|0a5|x}.

entries.name: Crimson Hall
entries: The Crimson Hall is the northern wing of the upper spire. Unless otherwise specified, the ceilings, doors, and lighting in the Crimson Hall are the same as in the rest of the upper spire, {@area as described in chapter 2|06b|x}.

entries.name: Crimson Hall Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 3.

entries.name: C1: Antechamber

entries: Blood-red light bathes this antechamber, filtering through large red windows. In the middle of the room, four Scourge-corrupted blood elves—three with pallid skin, one only bones—stand around a small glowing orb on a pedestal, taking turns drawing energy from it in a stream of blood-red magic. Opposite the entrance, a short flight of stairs leads up to a sealed door.
These elite San'layn include three nobles (Medium {@creature Vampire Nightbringer|XMM|Vampire Nightbringers}) and one adviser ({@creature Lich|XMM}).

A creature within 10 feet of the blood orb in the center of the room can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to draw power from it. The creature gains 20 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and deals double damage with all its attacks until the end of its next turn. Once a creature uses the orb in this way, the orb can't be used again until the end of the creature's next turn.
The last vampire to act uses the orb on the first round of combat if available. The lich doesn't use it.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating these guardians increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 1. The death of the lich also causes the door to swing open.

entries.name: C2: Hall of the Blood Prince Council

entries.title: Valanar, Taldaram, Keleseth
entries.credit: Left to right: Arthur Bozonnet, Arthur Gimaldinov, Vladimir Kafanov

entries: Three huge windows in the back of this cavernous room offer views into remote locations—nerubian caverns, a floating necropolis, and a vrykul-made keep, all bathed in red light that fills the room with shifting shadows. Three bodies lie lifeless on the dais before these windows.

The face of an undead blood elf, adorned with an elaborate headdress that suggests the ears of a bat, appears in the center window, and she laughs. "Foolish mortals," she says, her voice seeming to come from all around. "You thought us defeated so easily? The San'layn are the Lich King's immortal soldiers! Now you shall face their might combined!" As she speaks, her shoulders and batlike wings appear in the windows to either side. "Rise up, brothers, and destroy our enemies!" she cries, and an orb of blood-red light descends upon the center corpse. Tendrils of energy flow to the other corpses, and all three twitch with unlife and stand upright.

The reinvigorated corpses are three princes of the San'layn—{@creature Prince Keleseth|ICC}, {@creature Prince Taldaram|ICC}, and {@creature Prince Valanar|ICC}—each of whom uses the {@area Darkfallen Blood Prince|0e7|x} stat block with their own unique actions. The characters might have faced and defeated these princes before in the places displayed in the windows behind them: Keleseth in Utgarde Keep, Taldaram in Ahn'kahet, and Valanar at Naxxanar. (If you are running this as a one-shot adventure, feel free to tell the players that their characters faced these villains as powerful commanders of the Scourge in Northrend.) Once the blood prince council is reanimated, the face and figure of {@creature Blood-Queen Lana'thel|ICC} disappears from the windows behind them.

An orb of blood-red energy—the Invocation of Blood in the princes' stat block—surrounds Prince Valanar at the start of the encounter and moves to a different vampire at the end of each of Valanar's turns.

The windows aren't actual portals but projected illusions. If they are broken, nothing but the solid walls of the citadel lies behind them. Similarly, nothing hurled at the windows can affect Blood-Queen Lana'thel while her image appears in them.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating the blood prince council increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Prince Valanar wears a {@item Thrice Fanged Signet|ICC}. Each of the other two princes wears a ruby-set titanium ring worth 7,500 GP. Each of the three princes also wields an elaborate staff worth 7,500 GP.

entries.name: Blood Prince Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against the blood prince council by interjecting some of the things the vampires say in the WoW raid:
{@b When the Invocation of Blood Falls on Valanar (Including at the Start of Combat).} "Naxxanar was merely a setback! With the power of the orb, Valanar will have his vengeance!"
{@b When the Invocation of Blood Falls on Keleseth.} "Such wondrous power! The Darkfallen Orb has made me invincible!"
{@b When the Invocation of Blood Falls on Taldaram.} "Tremble before Taldaram, mortals, for the power of the orb flows through me!"
{@b When Keleseth Casts Hunger of Hadar.} "Blood will flow."
{@b When Taldaram Uses Glittering Sparks.} "Delight in the pain!"
{@b When Valanar Uses Kinetic Bomb.} "My cup runneth over."
{@b If a Character Drops to 0 Hit Points.} "Beg for mercy!"
{@b When Valanar Dies.} "... why?..."
{@b When Keleseth Dies.} "My queen, they... come."
{@b When Taldaram Dies.} "Worm... food."

entries.name: C3: The Antechamber of Blood
entries: Two ramps circle up from area C2, leading to this antechamber directly above that area.

Four aristocratic-looking undead elves stand guard in this antechamber, one wielding a blade wreathed in blood magic. Down the stairs beyond them, the bat-winged figure you saw in the windows below sits comfortably on a throne, watching with interest as the elves confront you.

The noble darkfallen in the antechamber are a blood knight (Medium {@creature Death Knight|XMM}), two archmages (Medium {@creature Vampire Umbral Lord|XMM|Vampire Umbral Lords}), and a noble (Medium {@creature Vampire Nightbringer|XMM}). {@creature Blood-Queen Lana'thel|ICC} watches the battle from area C4, but she doesn't interfere. However, if the characters try to leave the area without confronting her, she pursues them.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating these guardians increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 1.

entries.name: C4: The Sanctum of Blood

entries: As the last guardian of the antechamber falls, the vampire queen rises to her feet. "You have made an unwise decision," she says softly as she moves to stand beside the spread-eagle form of a dwarf—presumably the Argent Crusade spy you've been sent to rescue—who is suspended in the air by bands of red light. She traces a sharp claw along the dwarf's chin, eliciting a whimper of pain, then turns to stare at you. "This ends now."
This is {@creature Blood-Queen Lana'thel|ICC},* leader of the San'layn and one of the Lich King's most trusted lieutenants.

In combat, Lana'thel uses her Blood Mirror Bonus Action on her first turn. She either targets the character carrying {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} or attacks that character after she has used Blood Mirror. Either case causes the weapon to absorb some of the blood magic (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction).

entries.name: Development
entries: Infiltrator Minchar (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Spy Master|XMM}) is held in place by magic near Lana'thel's throne. The magic holding him captive is a version of the {@spell Imprisonment|XPHB} spell, with the lines of blood magic holding him instead of chains in the ground. Speaking or signing the passphrase "Know my hunger" while within this chamber ends the spell.

Defeating Blood-Queen Lana'thel increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 3. Lana'thel's resting place is a secret chamber hidden deep inside Icecrown Citadel. Finding it and destroying Lana'thel permanently is beyond the scope of this adventure.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Blood-Queen Lana'thel wears a {@item Bauble of True Blood|ICC} on a titanium chain around her neck (the chain alone is worth 7,500 GP). She also wields a rod (also worth 7,500 GP) tipped with glowing green crystals. An unlocked chest in the room holds 25,000 PP, a ruby-studded statuette of Minchar (the Material component used to bind him, worth 5,000 GP), seventy-five gemstones of various kinds (worth 1,000 GP each), ten shards of primordial saronite (worth 2,500 GP each), and eleven frost lotuses (rare {@book herbalism|WoW|3|Herbalism} resources worth 2,500 GP each; see the "{@area Crafting Resources|013|x}" sidebar in the introduction).

entries.name: More Blood-Queen Lana'thel Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Lana'thel by interjecting some of the things she says in the WoW raid:
{@b When She Uses Pact of the Darkfallen.} "Can you handle this?"
{@b When She Casts {@spell Dominate Monster|XPHB}.} "Yes... Feed, my precious one! You are mine now!"
{@b When She Casts {@spell Hunger of Hadar|XPHB}.} "Suffer!"
{@b If a Character Is Reduced to 0 Hit Points.} "Really? Is that all you've got?"
{@b When She Is Reduced to 0 Hit Points.} "But we were getting along so well..."

entries.name: Ending the Chapter
entries: When the characters defeat {@creature Blood-Queen Lana'thel|ICC} and free Infiltrator Minchar, award them each 8,700 XP. (Alternatively, advance each character to level 19.) In addition, each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} increases by 4. The characters can use the transporter at {@area area P4|07e|x} to return to Light's Hammer and rest.

data.name: Chapter 4: Frostwing Hall
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 19 Characters}

entries.name: Quests and Objectives
entries: The characters have the following tasks to complete in this chapter:

items.name: Final Barrier
items.entry: The last obstacle between the Ashen Verdict and the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King} is Arthas's mount, the undead dragon {@creature Sindragosa|ICC}.

items.name: Free Valithria
items.entry: The Scourge captured a dragon of the {@book green dragonflight|WoW|7|Green Dragonflight}, Valithria Dreamwalker, and are using her as a test subject in some grim experiment. If she is freed, she can help the characters defeat Sindragosa.

items.name: Respite for a Tormented Soul
items.entry: The most important information Valithria provides is that Sindragosa's soul isn't lost. When freed, Valithria provides the characters with life crystals that can capture Sindragosa's soul and usher it to its final rest.

items.name: Frost Infusion
items.entry: To infuse {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} with frost magic, the characters need to infuse some of Sindragosa's power into the blade.

entries.name: Beginning the Chapter
entries: After the characters rest from their efforts in {@adventure chapter 3|ICC|3}, Darion Mograine shares with them what he has learned about the final wing of the upper spire. Death knight scouts of the Ebon Blade reported that {@creature Sister Svalna|ICC} guards that wing. Svalna is a val'kyr, an ascended vrykul who wields formidable power in the service of the Scourge, and the death knight scouts knew her from their time in the Scourge. While taunting them from a distance, she informed them that the Lich King's servants are attempting to corrupt a dragon of the {@book green dragonflight|WoW|7|Green Dragonflight}, Valithria Dreamwalker, implying that there would soon be another {@creature frost wyrm|ICC} protecting this wing of the citadel.
Darion and Tirion ask the adventurers to slay Sister Svalna, free the green dragon, and destroy {@creature Sindragosa|ICC}—the last barrier between them and the Lich King himself.
Chapter 4 begins when the characters enter {@area area F1|0bb|x}.

entries.name: Frostwing Hall
entries: Frostwing Hall is the eastern wing of the upper spire. Unless otherwise specified, the ceilings, doors, and lighting in Frostwing Hall are the same as in the rest of the upper spire, {@area as described in chapter 2|06b|x}.

entries.name: Frostwing Hall Locations
entries: The following locations are keyed to map 4.

entries.name: F1: Frostwing Gauntlet

entries: A blue-skinned angelic being whose face is covered by a horned helmet hovers at the end of a long hallway, guarded by a pair of grotesque abominations. "Come!" the val'kyr shouts. "Your death approaches!"

The val'kyr is {@creature Sister Svalna|ICC},* and her bodyguards are two {@creature Abomination|WoW|Abominations}. The abominations rush down the hall toward the characters while Svalna remains at the end of the hall making attacks from range. If she can get three or more characters in the area of a Divine Surge, she uses that action; otherwise, she makes Bone Spear attacks. If a character dies in the hall, Svalna casts {@spell Create Undead|XPHB} on her next turn to raise the character as a {@creature Ghoul|XMM}.

When the abominations are slain, Sister Svalna retreats to the south ({@area area F2|0c2|x}). When she does, the Lich King's voice echoes throughout the Frostwing Hall, saying, "Intruders have breached the inner sanctum. Hasten the destruction of the green dragon! Leave only bones and sinew for the reanimation!"

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating Sister Svalna, either here or in area F2, increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2.

entries.name: More Sister Svalna Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Svalna by interjecting some of the things she says in the WoW raid:
{@b On the Abominations' First Turn.} "You must not approach the frost queen! Quickly, stop them!"
{@b The First Time She Uses Divine Surge.} "Miserable creatures. Die!"
{@b If a Character Is Reduced to 0 Hit Points.} "What? You die so easily? No matter."
{@b When She Dies.} "Perhaps... you were right..."

entries.name: F2: Frostwing Hall

entries: An enormous green dragon is huddled on the floor of this cavernous room, surrounded by spinning magical sigils traced in sapphire light. Two liches flank the imprisoned dragon, their bony hands extended, apparently pouring magical energy into maintaining the bonds. The dragon's eyes fix on you, and a hint of a smile twitches in the corner of her mouth. "Heroes, lend me your aid," she says in a pained voice. "I cannot hold them off much longer. You must heal my wounds!"

Valithria Dreamwalker is a {@creature Green Dragonflight Dragon (Gargantuan)|WoW|Green Dragonflight Dragon} who is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, with 111 Hit Points. Two {@creature Lich|XMM|Liches} have new orders to kill the dragon, but the arrival of the characters distracts them from that task. Along with {@creature Sister Svalna|ICC}* if she escaped here, the liches fight to keep the characters from advancing further. During combat, Svalna and the liches try to include Valithria in harmful areas of effect (such as Svalna's Divine Surge or the liches' {@spell Chain Lightning|XPHB} and other spells), hoping to finish her off while also killing the adventurers.

Valithria's magical bonds keep her from moving or taking any of the actions in her stat block. The one thing she can do is open a portal to the Emerald Dream, which she does on her first turn. The portal appears as a glowing green doorway shimmering in the air within 20 feet of her. A character can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to step through this portal, entering a lush green landscape where only Valithria and any characters who have entered her portal are present. A character remains here in the Emerald Dream until the end of the character's next turn. When a character in the Emerald Dream would normally roll one or more dice to restore Hit Points to a creature with a spell or other effect, instead use the highest number possible for each die. The dream version of Valithria here can use her Emerald Restoration Bonus Action on characters who are here with her.
If Valithria is healed to her Hit Point maximum (222 HP), she immediately breaks her bonds and helps the characters finish off any remaining foes.

entries.name: Development
entries: Once Valithria is freed and the enemies in this room defeated, Valithria takes on her high elf visage and asks the characters to show mercy to Sindragosa:

"The soul of a dragon is precious," Valithria says, "and even Sindragosa's is not utterly lost. Take these life crystals. They contain potent energy from the Emerald Dragonshrine in Dragonblight—which was my own secret to resisting the dark magic of this place for so long." She sighs.

When you face Sindragosa, battle her until she is weakened, and then use these crystals to coax out the essence that is dormant within her. If you then defeat her, you should be able to recover it and return it to Wyrmrest Temple in Dragonblight. Please do this, not for me, but for all dragonkind.

Freeing Valithria increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 2. Returning Sindragosa's crystalline essence to Wyrmrest Temple increases each character's Renown Score with the {@book Valdrakken Accord|WoW|4|Valdrakken Accord} by 5. That journey is beyond the scope of this adventure.

A lift to the south of this room constantly moves between this floor and {@area area F3|0c7|x} below. It spends 1 minute descending 100 feet to the floor of F3, remains there for another minute, then spends 1 minute ascending back here, waits another minute, and continues this cycle indefinitely. The lift is a metal disk 25 feet in diameter that magically raises and lowers without any visible support or mechanism.

entries.name: More Valithria Quotes
entries: Spice up the attempt to rescue Valithria by interjecting some of the things she says in the WoW raid:
{@b When She Opens a Portal to the Emerald Dream.} "I have opened a portal into the Dream. Your salvation lies within!"
{@b When She Is Healed to 167 Hit Points or More.} "My strength is returning! Press on, heroes!"
{@b If She Drops to 55 Hit Points or Fewer.} "I will not last much longer!"
{@b If She Is Fully Healed.} "I am renewed! Ysera, grant me the favor to lay these foul creatures to rest!"

entries.name: F3: Frost Queen's Antechamber

entries: A huge, vaulted chamber opens to the north of the lift. A passage continuing north is blocked by a metal portcullis.
If characters look up, they see massive chains running from the tops of the walls to the center of the ceiling, where they are choked with thick spiderwebs. Several large shapes move amid the webs.

When all the characters have entered the room, five {@creature Nerubian Crypt Fiend|WoW|Nerubian Crypt Fiends} descend from the ceiling to intercept them, hissing, "You must not approach the Frost Queen!"
When the nerubians are defeated, the portcullis on the far side of the room glides open. Defeating these guardians increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 1.

entries.name: F4: Frost Queen's Lair

entries: Past the portcullis is an antechamber with a wide balcony beyond. Two passages lead to the east and west, while the balcony looks out across the forbidding mountains of Icecrown. Two huge frost wyrms—undead dragons animated by the Scourge—circle in the air about a hundred feet away, while two Scourge giants watch over broods of ghostly dragon whelps.

On the balcony when the characters arrive are two frostwardens ({@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} with the Undead type) and eight frostwing whelps ({@creature White Dragon Wyrmling|XMM|White Dragon Wyrmlings} with the Undead type). These whelps are the spirits of Sindragosa's brood, which Arthas killed and raised into undeath in front of the dragon to break her will.

On the third round of combat, the two {@creature Frost Wyrm|ICC|Frost Wyrms},* Rimefang and Spinestalker, alight on the balcony and join the fray. When both frost wyrms are slain, the second one cries out in death with an echoing roar, and the voice of Sindragosa bellows from afar: "You are fools to have come to this place. The icy winds of Northrend will consume your souls!" {@creature Sindragosa|ICC}* lands on the balcony {@dice 1d4} rounds later.

When Sindragosa becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, each character holding one of Valithria Dreamwalker's life crystals feels the crystal stir to life. A character holding a life crystal can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to attune the crystal to Sindragosa's soul. A beam of greenish light connects the dragon to the crystal for 1 minute. If four or more crystals are connected to Sindragosa when she dies, her soul crystallizes into a clear crystal with a cloud of glimmering frost swirling inside it.

If a character holding {@item Shadow's Edge|ICC} (see "{@area Shadowmourne|03c|x}" in the introduction) is in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of Sindragosa's Frost Breath or targeted by her Ice Tombs, the weapon absorbs some of the frost energy, reducing the Cold damage the character takes that turn by {@dice 2d6}.

entries.name: Development
entries: Defeating Sindragosa increases each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} by 4.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Sindragosa's hoard is piled in the eastern alcove off the antechamber. It includes 44,000 PP; 200,000 GP; forty gems of various kinds worth 1,000 GP each; fifteen gems of various kinds worth 5,000 GP each; fifty shards of primordial saronite (worth 2,500 GP each); a {@item Sundial of Eternal Dusk|ICC}; a {@item Robe of the Archmagi|XDMG}; a {@item Ring of Spell Turning|XDMG}; a {@item +3 Shield|XDMG}; {@item Boots of Speed|XDMG}; an {@item Ioun Stone, Intellect|XDMG|Ioun Stone} (intellect); and two {@item Potion of Mana (Superior)|WoW|Potions of Mana} (superior).

entries.name: More Sindragosa Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against Sindragosa by interjecting some of the things she says in the WoW raid:
{@b When She Uses Her Unchained Magic Reaction.} "Suffer, mortals, as your pathetic magic betrays you!"
{@b The First Time She Uses Her Blistering Cold Bonus Action.} "Can you feel the cold hand of death upon your heart?"
{@b When She Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.} "Enough! I tire of these games!"
{@b When a Character Activates One of Valithria's Life Crystals After Sindragosa Is Bloodied.} "Aaah! It burns! What sorcery is this?"
{@b When She Uses Ice Tombs.} "Your incursion ends here! None shall survive!"
{@b If a Character Is Reduced to 0 Hit Points.} "A flaw of mortality..."
{@b When She Dies.} "Free... at last..."

entries.name: F5: Sindragosa's Lair Transporter

entries: An arcane sigil in a circular frame, identical to the one at the citadel's entrance, seems to stir with life as you approach.
This transporter works exactly like the one in {@area area H1|00e|x}.

entries.name: Ending the Chapter
entries: When the characters free Valithria and defeat {@creature Sindragosa|ICC}, award them each 17,200 XP. (Alternatively, advance each character to level 20.) In addition, each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} increases by 4.
Once Sindragosa and all the other bosses of the citadel are defeated, the transporter in {@area area P5|080|x} is activated, allowing characters access to {@adventure the Frozen Throne|ICC|5}.

data.name: Chapter 5: The Frozen Throne
entries: {@i An Adventure for Level 20 Characters}

entries.name: Quests and Objectives
entries: The characters have the following tasks to complete in this chapter:

items.name: Save Bolvar Fordragon
items.entry: The renowned commander who led the Alliance forces at the Wrathgate is still alive, suffering unimaginable torment at Arthas's hands. The characters must free him.

items.name: The Lich King Is Dead
items.entry: The assault on Icecrown Citadel has all been for this: {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Arthas} must die to put an end to the horror of {@book the Scourge|WoW|6|The Scourge}.

items.name: Long Live the Lich King
items.entry: A masterless Scourge would be worse than one that marches at the Lich King's command. Someone of noble heart must don Arthas's {@item Helm of Domination|WoW} and keep a tight rein on the Scourge.

entries.name: Beginning the Chapter
entries: After {@creature Sindragosa|ICC|Sindragosa's} destruction, the leaders of the Ashen Verdict encourage the adventurers to quickly prepare for the final assault on the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King}. Assuming all the requirements have been met, Highlord Darion Mograine finishes forging {@item Shadowmourne|ICC}, a worthy weapon to bring about Arthas's defeat. Either King Varian Wrynn of Stormwind or Warlord Garrosh Hellscream of Orgrimmar provides a Blessing to the adventurers (see "{@area Leaders' Blessings|0d4|x}" below). And Highlord {@creature Tirion Fordring|ICC},* one of the paladins who first inducted young Arthas Menethil into the Order of the Silver Hand, accompanies the characters to the Frozen Throne.

When all the dungeon bosses except Arthas are dead, the teleporter in the center of the upper spire ({@area area P5|080|x}) activates, allowing transport to the Frozen Throne. {@area As described in chapter 2|06b|x}, the two {@creature Val'kyr Herald|ICC|Val'kyr Heralds}* that guard the upper spire try to prevent the characters from reaching the transporter.

entries.name: Leaders' Blessings
entries: Before ascending the Frozen Throne, Alliance characters receive a supernatural gift called {@reward Strength of Wrynn|ICC}, while Horde characters receive one called {@reward Hellscream's Warsong|ICC}. The effects of these Blessings are identical:

entries.name: The Frozen Throne
entries: The Frozen Throne is the top of the pillar of ice that runs the height of the spire of Icecrown Citadel. At its pinnacle, Arthas has hewn a throne from which he commands the forces of the Scourge. Before the throne stands a huge platform of ice-covered saronite and stone, swept by the frozen winds of Icecrown's mountainous heights.

entries.name: Frozen Throne Features
entries: The Frozen Throne is an open-air location with no artificial light, no doors, and no ceiling.

entries.name: Frozen Throne Locations
entries: The Frozen Throne is shown on map 5.

entries.name: Throne Room of the Lich King

entries: The transporter deposits you at the pinnacle of Icecrown Citadel, a dizzying height above the entrance. Four jagged spires surround this platform like icy talons, and a ring of saronite engraved with arcane runes is embedded in the ice-covered floor.

On the south side of the platform, the pillar of ice that runs up the center of the entire spire emerges from the building and rises to a sharp point overhead. A rough staircase hewn from the ice leads to a throne where the Lich King sits motionless. Above the throne, a human figure—scorched and scarred—hangs spread-eagle between two tall pillars.
Tirion Fordring's voice thrums with excitement. "Long have I waited for this day, heroes. Are you prepared to bring the Lich King to justice? We charge on your command!"
The Lich King's chuckle, carried on the wind or perhaps voiced directly in your mind, drips with scorn.
The location of the transporter is marked {@i A} on the map. The Frozen Throne, with Bolvar Fordragon's broken body suspended above it, is marked {@i B}.

{@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW} remains on the Frozen Throne and taunts his former commander as the characters approach. "So the Light's vaunted justice has finally arrived?" he says. "Shall I lay down {@i Frostmourne} and throw myself at your mercy, Fordring?" Only then does he stand and descend the stairs. Because the Lich King is at the seat of his power, he has 4 Legendary Action uses each round instead of 3. He can also cast {@spell Create Undead|XPHB} at any hour of the day, not just at night.

{@creature Tirion Fordring|ICC}* fights alongside the characters through this encounter. His stat block is simple, making it easy for you to run him in combat, but you can also let one of the players play as him or let the players take turns making his attack rolls.

entries.name: Frostmourne
entries: If a character's soul is trapped in {@item Frostmourne|WoW} by Arthas's Soul Reaper, read the following text to the player:

Your soul is torn from your body, and oblivion swallows you—for a moment. Then dim light reaches your eyes again, and you find yourself in a nightmarish inversion of the Frozen Throne, draped in darkness. Two shining white wraith-like creatures are locked in battle with a regal figure you don't recognize, who calls out to you. "You have come to bring Arthas to justice? First, you must escape {@i Frostmourne's} hold or be damned as I am: trapped within this cursed blade for all eternity. Aid me in destroying these tortured souls! Together we will loosen {@i Frostmourne's} hold and weaken the Lich King from within!"

The wraith-like creatures are spirit wardens (use the {@creature Death Slaad|XMM} stat block), embodiments of the magic that imprisons souls inside {@i Frostmourne}. The spirit battling the wardens is Terenas Menethil, Arthas's father (Medium, Lawful Good {@creature Questing Knight|XMM} who is currently {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, with 101 Hit Points). The dead character has half their Hit Point maximum (round down) and access to all their capabilities and equipment as if they hadn't died.

If additional characters are trapped in {@i Frostmourne}, they appear in the same place and can join the fight against the spirit wardens. If the spirit wardens are defeated, all slain characters, as well as Terenas Menethil, reappear on the battlefield, their Hit Points unchanged from what they were inside the blade. (Terenas remains a spirit, though his game statistics are unchanged, while fallen characters return to their bodies.) From that point, Arthas can't use the Soul Reaper effect of his Frostmourne action, and he has only 3 Legendary Action uses each round.
If a character dies inside the blade, their soul is lost, and only the {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell can return them to life.

entries.name: Arthas Bloodied
entries: When Arthas becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, the area shakes with a mighty earthquake. Each creature on the ground except Arthas makes a {@dc 23} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and its {@status Concentration|XPHB} is broken. In addition, the edges of the platform—everything outside the roughly circular shape marked with blue fissures on the map—crumble and fall to the ground below. A character within 5 feet of a safe edge can leap to safety with a successful {@dc 23} Dexterity saving throw, landing at the new edge of the platform with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Characters who fail that save or are farther from the safe edges fall 500 feet.

entries.name: The Lich King's Final Effort
entries: At the end of the turn in which he is reduced to 125 Hit Points or fewer, Arthas uses his Remorseless Winter Legendary Action (even if he has already used it this round) and gloats over the characters for a moment. "You truly are Azeroth's greatest champions. And Tirion has delivered you right into my hands, exactly as I intended."

entries.name: Divine Intervention
entries: If the characters are on the verge of defeat, Tirion (together with Terenas if he has been freed from Frostmourne) calls on the Light for aid. A wave of Holy Light washes over the party, with one of the following effects (your choice):

items: The Light removes all {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels from the party.
The Light restores all dead characters to life, even those whose souls were lost to {@i Frostmourne}.
The Light restores up to 700 Hit Points to the party, distributed as evenly as possible.

entries.name: Death of the Lich King
entries: At the conclusion of the MMO raid, the characters are briefly rendered helpless and forced to watch as Tirion brings about the Lich King's defeat. Arthas's use of Remorseless Winter when he is near death and Tirion's access to divine intervention are nods to that script, but you're encouraged to let the characters (and the dice) determine the outcome of this battle.
If you want to, you can narrate the final interaction between the dying Lich King and the spirit of his father:
The spirit of Terenas materializes over the Lich King's fallen form and cradles his son's head in his arms.
"Father?" Arthas breathes. "Is it... over?"
At long last. No king rules forever, my son.
With his final breaths, Arthas gasps, "I see... only darkness... before me." And he is gone.

Terenas stands and fixes his gaze on Tirion. "Without its master's command, the restless Scourge will become an even greater threat to this world. Control must be maintained. There must always be a Lich King."
In a flash of light, the spirit is gone, and Tirion stands, looking down at Arthas's helm.

entries.name: Bolvar Fordragon
entries: Bolvar Fordragon, the commander of the Alliance forces at the Wrathgate (see "{@area Battle of the Wrathgate|005|x}" in the introduction), hangs suspended above the Lich King's throne at the start of this encounter. When Arthas dies, Bolvar's chains release him, and he falls to the ground at the foot of the Frozen Throne. He was badly burned by the purging flames of the red dragonflight at the Wrathgate, and his body has been further broken by the Lich King's tortures. Even so, he slowly crawls up onto the Frozen Throne until he sits on it as Arthas did. See "{@area Ending the Adventure|0e4|x}" for Bolvar's fate.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: In addition to {@item Frostmourne|WoW} and the {@item Helm of Domination|WoW}, the Lich King keeps a small chest of souvenirs near the Frozen Throne. Inside are the following treasures:

items: A vial of blood taken from the dying {@creature Sylvanas Windrunner|WoW}
An {@item Amulet|XPHB|Amulet of Faith}, which was Arthas's badge of office as a paladin, given to him by Uther the Lightbringer
A simple, heavily worn {@item Longsword|XPHB} that Arthas used in his training with Muradin Bronzebeard
A locket with the image of {@creature Jaina Proudmoore|WoW} engraved inside
A large crystal holding a shard of the soul of Highlord Alexandros Mograine, Darion Mograine's father

entries: Returning these items (except the reins) to the people connected to them would be an errand of mercy—but it is beyond the scope of this adventure.

entries.name: More Arthas Quotes
entries: Spice up combat against the Lich King by interjecting some of the things he says in the WoW raid:
{@b At the Start of Combat.} "When my work is complete, you will beg for mercy—and I will deny you. Your anguished cries will be testament to my unbridled power."
{@b The First Time He Uses Remorseless Winter.} "I will freeze you from within until all that remains is an icy husk."
{@b When He Becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.} "Watch as the world around you collapses!"
{@b If He Uses Soul Reaper on a Character.} "{@i Frostmourne} hungers!"
{@b The First Time He Casts Finger of Death.} "Face now your tragic end!"
{@b The First Time He Uses His Defile Reaction.} "Hope wanes..."

entries.name: Ending the Adventure
entries: Tirion is ready to make the ultimate sacrifice, becoming the new Lich King to contain the power of the Scourge. But Bolvar intercedes, demanding that Tirion place the {@item Helm of Domination|WoW} upon Bolvar's head instead. The characters can interrupt their conversation and make a case for one or the other of the paladins—or one of the adventurers—to wear the crown.

Award the characters 90,000 XP for defeating the {@creature Lich King Arthas|WoW|Lich King} in his lair, plus 22,000 XP as a story award for defeating the Lich King and placing a new one on the Frozen Throne. In addition, each character's Renown Score with the {@area Ashen Verdict|026|x} increases by 7.
